senses.gloss:
उक्ष् 1. उक्ष्, cl. 1. 6. P. A. उक्षति, -ते,
उक्षाञ्-चकार (Ved. ववक्ष, -षे),
उक्षितुम्, to sprinkle, moisten, wet; to sprinkle or
scatter in small drops, to emit; to throw out, scatter
(as sparks); to clean; [cf. Lith. ûkana: Hib. uisg,
uisge, ‘water, a river;’ uisgeach, ‘aquatic, watery,
fluid, moist, pluvial.’]

उक्ष् 2. उक्ष्, cl. 1. P., Ved. उक्षति,
ववक्ष, and A. ववक्षे, उक्षितुम्,
to grow up, to grow strong; A. to strengthen one's
self; become strong: Caus. उक्षयते, -यितुम्, to
strengthen.

1. उक्ष, अस्, m. (at the end of some compounds)
= उक्षन् below; (अस्, आ, अम्), clean (?).

उक्षण्य, nom. P., Ved. उक्षण्यति, to do or
behave like Ukṣan; (Sāy.) to desire one who pours
down riches &c.

उक्षण्यायन, अस्, m., Ved. a patronymic from
Ukṣaṇya.

उक्षण्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. behaving or doing like
Ukṣan; (Sāy.) desirous of one who pours down
riches &c.

उक्षन्, आ, m. an ox or bull (especially as drawing
the chariot of Uṣas or dawn); epithet of the Soma
(as sprinkling or scattering small drops); of the
Maruts; of the sun and Agni; one of the eight chief
medicaments (ऋषभ); N. of a man; (आ, आ, अ),
large (?); [cf. Zend ukhṣan; Goth. auhsa and
auhsu; Armen. eṣn.]
—उक्ष-तर, अस्, m. a small
bull or ox; a large bull.
—उक्ष-वश, अस्, m., Ved.
a bull-calf, male calf.
—उक्ष-वेहत्, अत्, m., Ved. an
impotent bull (?).
—उक्षान्न (˚क्ष-अन्˚), अस्, आ,
अम्, Ved. one whose food is oxen.

1. उक्षित, अस्, आ, अम्, sprinkled, moistened,
cleansed, perfumed.

2. उक्षित, अस्, आ, अम्, adult, of full growth, strong;
old.

उक्षाल, अस्, आ, अम् (?), swift, excellent, terrible,
high, much; (अस्), m. a monkey (?).
